evals.name: setup-ask-first
evals.prompt: I want proper changelogs and version management in this repo (tasklet, a little Python CLI). Every change should get logged somewhere as we go, and when I release, it should all become a real changelog entry with the version bumped. Set it up — you have my go-ahead to create whatever files are needed — and backfill what's changed since the last release (v0.3.0). Don't install any git hooks and don't tag anything.
evals.expected_output: The agent inspects the repo (init --dry-run) and then asks, in one message, how versions should look (with examples from 0.3.0), which kinds of releases they make, and how releases happen (by hand or automatically on merge/PR); it creates nothing until answered.
assertions: Asks how versions should look and which kinds of releases they make, with concrete examples built from the current version 0.3.0
Asks how releases happen (by hand, or automatically on each merge or PR)
Waits for the answers: no changelog system is created yet (no new files at all)
No commits, git hooks or tags

evals.name: log-after-commit
evals.prompt: I just committed the CSV export feature for reports. Log it in the changelog please.
evals.expected_output: One user-facing fragment in .changelog/unreleased/ (type added) naming the CSV export commit; no CHANGELOG.md edit, no bump; status clean afterwards.
assertions: A new changelog entry mentions CSV export
The entry is a fragment in .changelog/unreleased/ (the repo's convention), and CHANGELOG.md was not created or edited
The fragment is typed as an addition (type: added)
The fragment references the CSV export commit
The entry is written for users: no internal function names (export_csv) or file paths
No version bump and no new tag
Afterwards no commit since the last release is uncovered (changelogger status shows no drafts)

evals.name: cut-release
evals.prompt: Let's cut a release. Pick the right version number, compile the changelog, and make the release commit — I'm fine with whatever version the changes call for. Don't tag or push anything.
evals.expected_output: 2.0.0 (breaking change) in both version files; new top section in CHANGELOG.md in the existing '## X — date' style with all 6 user-relevant changes incl. the 2 commits that had no fragment; older sections intact; whats-new.json without the internal uv entry; fragments archived; release commit; no tag.
assertions: Version is 2.0.0 in both pyproject.toml and src/reportly/__init__.py
CHANGELOG.md has a 2.0.0 section above 1.4.2, in the file's existing heading style (## 2.0.0 — YYYY-MM-DD)
The hand-written 1.4.2 and 1.4.1 sections are preserved verbatim
The two commits that had no fragment (PDF fonts fix, --quiet flag) appear in the 2.0.0 notes
Dropping Python 3.8 is called out as breaking
web/whats-new.json lists 2.0.0 first and leaves out the internal uv build entry
Fragments are archived: none left in .changelog/unreleased/, changelog.json lists 2.0.0 first
A release commit exists and the working tree is clean
No new tag was created
Reply asks (or records as questions) which changes the release should lead with and how detailed the notes should be

evals.name: hotfix-scheme
evals.prompt: We version this app as v1.4, v1.5 and so on — just major.minor — and when an urgent fix has to go out on top of a release we ship it as a hotfix, like v1.4.hotfix-1. Set up changelogs and versioning that way, then ship the fix I just committed as a hotfix release. The release commit is enough — don't tag or push.
evals.expected_output: Versioning set to {major}.{minor}[.hotfix-{hotfix}]; package.json stores a valid, non-pre-release SemVer for the hotfix (1.4.0+hotfix.1 or 1.4.1); CHANGELOG.md gets a 1.4.hotfix-1 section describing the session-expiry fix for users; the scheme is recorded for future releases; release commit; no tag.
assertions: The release is named 1.4.hotfix-1 in a CHANGELOG.md heading
package.json holds a valid SemVer that is not a pre-release and is newer than 1.4.0 in intent (e.g. 1.4.0+hotfix.1 or 1.4.1; not 1.4.0-hotfix.1, which sorts before 1.4.0)
The hotfix entry describes the session-expiry fix from the user's point of view (no file paths or function names)
The versioning scheme (major.minor plus hotfixes) is recorded in the repo for future releases
A release commit exists and the working tree is clean
No new tag was created (only v1.4)

evals.name: setup-answered
evals.prompt: Set up changelogs and version management in this repo (tasklet, a little Python CLI) so every change gets logged as we go and releases turn it into a real changelog with the version bumped. We use plain SemVer with the v only in tags, and releases are manual — I tell you when to cut one. Backfill what's changed since v0.3.0. Don't install git hooks and don't tag anything.
evals.expected_output: SemVer set up without re-asking; pyproject.toml + src/tasklet/__init__.py as version files; polished fragments for the 4 user-visible commits; nothing bumped; no hooks/tags; What's new proposal.
assertions: All four user-visible changes since v0.3.0 are logged (--due filter, empty tasks.json fix, gist sync, missing task file message)
Internal commits are not logged as entries (no mention of the ruff bump or the due-date test)
No logged entry is left as a raw draft (no 'draft: true', no conventional-commit prefixes like 'feat(' or 'fix:')
Version management knows both version locations (a new config/script/doc references pyproject.toml and src/tasklet/__init__.py)
Nothing was bumped: both version files still say 0.3.0 and ruff's target-version is untouched
No git hooks installed and no new tags
Reply proposes a place where end users can see changes (What's new / release notes)

evals.name: ci-automation
evals.prompt: This repo already keeps its changelog with changelogger. We want releases to be automatic from now on: every merge to main should bump the version, update the changelog and tag the release, and pull requests should fail if they don't include a changelog entry. Set that up with GitHub Actions. Commit the setup, but don't push anything.
evals.expected_output: Vendored script + two workflows (PR check via `check --range`, release on push to main via `release auto --tag` with loop guard and contents: write); setup committed; no push/tag; reply warns about protected branches / GITHUB_TOKEN not triggering other workflows.
assertions: A pull_request workflow checks that every change has a changelog entry
A workflow on pushes to main bumps the version, updates the changelog and tags the release
The release workflow cannot loop on its own release commits
The release workflow has permission to push (contents: write)
Every script the workflows run exists in the repo
The setup is committed and nothing was tagged
Reply warns what the default GITHUB_TOKEN cannot do (push to protected branches, trigger other workflows from its tags)
